summary: No. 3 Michigan beat No. 10 Penn State 24-15 at Beaver Stadium under acting coach Sherrone Moore, using a run-heavy, conservative game plan while Jim Harbaugh was barred from the sideline. The Big Ten's ruling over the sign-stealing scandal keeps Harbaugh off the field for the final three regular-season games, pending a Nov. 17 restraining order hearing. The author argues Michigan won't be able to beat No. 1 Ohio State the same way on Nov. 25 and still needs Harbaugh for that game.
one_line: Michigan beat Penn State 24-15 under acting coach Sherrone Moore, but the author argues the Wolverines need Harbaugh against Ohio State.
key_facts: No. 3 Michigan beat No. 10 Penn State 24-15 at Beaver Stadium on Saturday, improving to 10-0 overall and 7-0 in the Big Ten.
Michigan threw one pass in the second half under acting coach Sherrone Moore, and it did not technically count because it drew a pass interference call on a throw to tight end Colston Loveland.
J.J. McCarthy finished 7 of 8 passing for 60 yards, and Michigan had 30 rushing attempts and zero passing attempts in the second half.
Blake Corum rushed 26 times for 145 yards and 2 TDs, including a 44-yard run and a 30-yard TD; Donovan Edwards had 10 carries for 52 yards and a TD.
Michigan trailed 3-0 after the first quarter, then led 14-9 at halftime; the Wolverines had eight carries for 10 yards in the first quarter.
Penn State quarterback Drew Allar went 10 of 22 for 70 yards and a TD, and the Nittany Lions had just one play of more than 20 yards.
Michigan's defense now allows just 7.5 points per game.
In a Fox postgame interview with Jenny Taft, Moore thanked Harbaugh and used profanity, saying 'I did this for you, for this university, the president, our AD.'

The Big Ten ruled Friday that Harbaugh cannot be on the field for the final three regular-season games because of the in-person scouting and sign-stealing scandal that led to staffer Conor Stalions' resignation.
ESPN reported a temporary restraining order hearing will take place on Nov. 17 to decide whether Harbaugh can be on the field.
Ohio State beat Penn State 20-12 on Oct. 21, with Heisman candidate Marvin Harrison Jr. as the separator, and has a top-five defense.
More than 17 million people watched last year's 45-23 Michigan win over Ohio State; early forecasts say 20 million will watch The Game this year, on Nov. 25.
Harbaugh reportedly watched the Penn State game from the team hotel.
